title: Dict patterns in match, private members, macros
description: match accepts {name, age: n, kind: literal} patterns (nested too); private fn / private a, b are compile-time private to the class (also hidden from subclasses); macro name(a) { ... } with name!(x) expands before compilation with expression arguments parenthesised.

title: eval and exec
description: eval(code, vars) and exec(code, vars) run text in a fresh VM under the caller capabilities (no new power; nesting limit 8). This closes the eval item that needed a security decision: it is built so that the sandbox still applies.

title: Matrix library
description: Matrix(rows), matrix_zeros, matrix_identity written in Killer (src/std/matrix.killer, auto-included): + - * scalar, product, transpose, det, inverse, solve, close.

title: SQL database
description: New src/sql_engine.rs (no dependencies): sql_open/sql_exec/sql_query/sql_close with CREATE/DROP/INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE, WHERE, GROUP BY, aggregates, ORDER BY, LIMIT/OFFSET, parameters, file persistence (atomic rewrite). No joins or subqueries.

title: Windows through the browser
description: gui_open(target) and gui_show(title, html, handlers) (src/std/gui.killer): serve a page on a free port, open the system browser, handle events by POST until quit(). No native widgets.

title: Step debugger
description: killer debug script [--break N]: step, next, finish, continue, breakpoints, list, call stack, locals (by slot/arg name), globals. Uses the VM hook that also turns the JIT off.

title: OPEN: not built
description: TLS listeners and wss:// (HTTPS client works through curl); WebAssembly output; SQL joins/subqueries; native GUI widgets; hygienic macros; live LLM provider tests (need a key); release workflow run (needs a tag).

title: TLS client sockets and wss://
description: tcp_connect_tls and ws_connect(wss://) through the system openssl s_client (certificate chain and host name verified; ca_file option; tls_error explains a failed check). Connection type generalised to a TCP/TLS stream. No TLS listener.

title: WebAssembly output
description: killer wasm compiles numeric functions (f64, if/while/for range, break/continue, recursion, math functions) to a .wasm module with no imports. Tested by a spec-based interpreter in tests/wasm.rs against the Killer VM.

title: OPEN: not built
description: TLS listeners (HTTPS servers); WebAssembly for strings, lists and objects; SQL joins and subqueries; native GUI widgets; hygienic macros; live LLM provider tests (need a key); release workflow run (needs a tag).

title: SQL joins and subqueries
description: sql_query now supports INNER, LEFT and CROSS JOIN (and comma joins) with ON and table aliases, qualified t.col names with ambiguity errors, subqueries (IN, scalar, EXISTS, FROM, correlated), HAVING, DISTINCT, COUNT(DISTINCT), BETWEEN, CASE, coalesce/ifnull/nullif/abs/round/upper/lower/length/substr, INSERT ... SELECT, three-valued NOT/AND/OR/IN. Not supported: RIGHT/FULL JOIN, USING, UNION, window functions. Cross-checked against Python sqlite3 (79 queries, 9 error cases). File format unchanged.

title: Hygienic macros
description: Names a macro body introduces (assignments, let/const, for/catch variables, lambda params) are renamed per expansion to _mN__name so they cannot capture or clobber caller variables; parameters, free names, members, keys and strings are untouched; $name in a body opts out. Tests: macro_hygiene, macro_error_lines in tests/language_additions.rs.

title: Opt-in live LLM provider tests, offline fake-server tests, llm.rs fixes
description: tests/llm_live.rs: offline_* tests run against a fake OpenAI-compatible / Anthropic / Ollama server (JSON, SSE, NDJSON, chunked, 401/404 errors) and check request path, headers, body, parsing, streaming and errors; live_* tests (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, embeddings, bad-key error path) run only when OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / a reachable Ollama is present and otherwise print skipped. Fixes in llm.rs: Ollama ignored base_url and OLLAMA_HOST, OpenAI embeddings ignored base_url, the inference cache ignored endpoint and key, Anthropic kept only the last system message, JSON unicode escapes were not decoded, Ollama error replies were reported as parse failures. Offline part done; the live run is pending an API key (docs/LLM_TESTING.md).

title: Release workflow and installer review
description: Fixed: workflow shipped killer_super (reports v4.0.0) instead of the killer driver (reports 1.0.0 = Cargo.toml); added tag-vs-Cargo.toml check, smoke test (--version and hello world), workflow_dispatch dry run that never publishes, branch-safe archive names, prerelease only for tags with a hyphen; installers now install killer and killer_super and accept KILLER_BASE_URL. Verified locally: release build, tar.gz and sha256 step, install.sh into a temp dir, checksum mismatch rejected, YAML parse. Not verified: install.ps1 and the zip step (PowerShell blocked here), any real GitHub run. See docs/RELEASING.md.

title: Native GUI widgets
description: window(title,w,h) with label/button/input/checkbox/list/combo, get/set, run() event loop, simulate_click and close hooks, message_box. Real Win32 controls on Windows through extern system declarations (no crate); in-memory headless model elsewhere or with KILLER_GUI_HEADLESS=1. Handlers run in Killer code on the VM thread. Never seen on a real screen; tests create hidden real windows.

title: WebAssembly strings and lists
description: killer wasm now compiles ASCII strings (literals in a data segment, concatenation, equality, indexing, len, for-in) and lists of numbers (literal, index, assignment, push, len, for-in) using a bump allocator in exported linear memory, with type inference plus string/array annotations and exported host helpers (killer_str_new, killer_list_get and so on). Numbers-only modules are unchanged (no memory). Tested by the extended spec-based interpreter in tests/wasm.rs (memory, loads, stores, i32 ops, traps) against the Killer VM. Still open: dicts and objects, str() and other builtins, lists of strings, non-ASCII text, freeing memory.

title: TLS server (HTTPS, wss:// listener)
description: tls_listen(addr, cert, key) / tls_accept(listener) return ordinary socket handles (sock_send, sock_recv, sock_recv_line, sock_close); ws_accept works on a TLS listener; serve(port, handler, {tls: {cert, key}}) serves HTTPS through a TLS front that forwards to a private loopback listener. One TLS terminator child per connection (openssl s_server; on Windows a PowerShell SslStream helper because the Windows openssl s_server blocks on piped stdin) with a bridge thread; credentials checked up front (openssl present, files parse, key matches certificate). Tested with curl and self-signed certs in tests/tls_server.rs.

title: x-- error, += in one-line blocks, TLS timeouts
description: x-- (a silent comment, endless while loop) is now a compile error telling you to write x -= 1; += -= *= /= %= and ++ work inside one-line blocks (for/while/if/else, nested). TLS helper flush ceiling 3 s to 20 s and wss handshake read timeout 10 s to 30 s after resets and timeouts under load; HTTPS test no longer burns its request budget on a retried attempt.

title: Archive 155 never-compiled files; fix port-reuse test flake
description: 155 .rs files that no mod/#[path] reaches moved with git mv to SOURCE/src/v2-rust/killer/archive/uncompiled (same relative paths, README explains; nothing deleted; build verified). tests free_port never returns the same port twice per process (Windows CI hit os error 10048 in streaming_profile).

title: TLS server: root cause of connection reset (curl 56)
description: Found with KILLER_TLS_DEBUG tracing under 4 parallel test runs. (1) serve() returned right after the last max_requests request and the process exit cut the TLS helper off before the reply was delivered (client saw a reset): serve now waits up to 15 s for TLS connections in flight. (2) The TLS front connected to the HTTP backend before the helper had a request, so under load the idle backend connection blocked the single-threaded loop and hit its 10 s read timeout (408): the front now connects only once the first plain-text bytes arrive. (3) The bridge closed the client socket with Shutdown::Both while the client still had unread data (RST discards the reply): it now half-closes and waits for the client FIN. The PowerShell helper drains a failed handshake instead of exiting with unread data. HTTPS test is strict again (max_requests 3, served 3, retries only on curl exit 7).

title: Absolute-path lookup for openssl/curl/powershell
description: New src/tool_path.rs resolves openssl and curl once to an absolute path: PATH entries that are empty, relative or the current directory are skipped, KILLER_OPENSSL / KILLER_CURL (absolute) override, PATH snapshot taken before the first env_set so scripts cannot redirect the helper, PowerShell from SystemRoot first, clear missing-tool error. Used by net_sock, net_tls_server, http_req, llm, llm_stream, image_gen, vision. Vision/Anthropic/Gemini/OpenAI calls no longer put API keys in argv (curl -K - on stdin); Windows PKCS#12 password per connection via env not argv. Trust model in SOURCE/docs/project/SECURITY.md.

title: eval/exec: caller capabilities, budget, warning
description: Real gap fixed: eval/exec ran in a fresh VM with the default trusted capability set, so a restricted script could use eval for file/network/process access; the VM now gets the caller capabilities. Also added 50M-step and 30 s limits (shared across nesting) so an endless loop in eval ends with an error, a warning box in LANGUAGE.md, and the FEATURES.md row note. No memory cap exists (documented).

title: Crypto audit against published test vectors
description: tests/crypto_vectors.rs (25 tests) plus unit tests check SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512 (FIPS 180), HMAC-SHA256 (RFC 4231 cases 1-7), PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (RFC 7914, 1/4096/80000 iterations), ChaCha20/Poly1305/AEAD (RFC 8439 incl. appendix A), base64 (RFC 4648), WebSocket accept key (RFC 6455) against the Rust functions, the Killer builtins and an independent Python reference (tests/data/crypto_reference.py). SHA-256, HMAC, PBKDF2, ChaCha20-Poly1305, SHA-1, base64 were already correct. Bugs fixed: encryption.rs was a fake (XOR cipher with an unchecked tag, XOR-fold hash, LCG keys) and is now real ChaCha20-Poly1305/SHA-512/PBKDF2 with OS random and errors for AES/SHA-3/Argon2; cryptography_solver aes_encrypt returned the plain text; hex_decode panicked on odd length; b64_decode and base64_decode accepted malformed input; compression_module base64 had no padding; uuid() used RandomState; PIN hash was unsalted SHA-256 compared with ==. docs/CRYPTO.md lists what is verified, what is not implemented and the limits (not audited, no side-channel guarantees).

title: Close curl -k; release notes warn about the old fake encryption
description: curl -k removed from llm.rs web-search fetchers and image_gen.rs (certificates verified, CURL_CA_BUNDLE for TLS-intercepting proxies, only http_request insecure:true turns checks off; tests/no_insecure_curl.rs guards it). docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md (wired into release.yml as body_path) and CHANGELOG carry the warning that the old encryption.rs XOR cipher did not encrypt.

title: insecure: true prints a warning
description: Every request run with insecure: true (http_request, embeddings, streaming LLM calls) prints one warning to stderr: certificate verification DISABLED for <host>. The warning names the host only, never the URL query. Unit test in http_req plus two end-to-end tests in tests/no_insecure_curl.rs.

title: Crypto moved to RustCrypto crates (first external dependencies)
description: Replaced the hand-written SHA-256 (builtin, android_security, ghost_vm_sha, encryption), SHA-512, HMAC-SHA256 (encryption, ghost_vm_sha, lang_builtins), PBKDF2, ChaCha20 and Poly1305 (aead.rs) with thin wrappers over chacha20poly1305 0.10, sha2 0.10, hmac 0.12, pbkdf2 0.12 and subtle 2 (default-features off); constant-time compares use subtle. Builtins, error messages and the KSE2 format unchanged; RFC 8439, RFC 4231, RFC 7914, FIPS 180 vectors and the Python interop tests pass. SHA-1 and base64 stay hand-written. README, DOCS, CRYPTO.md, FEATURES, LANGUAGE, ARCHITECTURE and CHANGELOG no longer claim zero external crates; CRYPTO.md says the crates are widely used and reviewed, Killer's integration is not audited.

title: Memory cap for eval/exec
description: eval and exec now run under a memory cap (default 256 MB; eval(code, vars, {"max_memory_mb": N}) or env KILLER_EVAL_MAX_MEMORY; 1 to 2048 MB). A thin counting wrapper around the system allocator (memcap.rs; one thread-local read per allocation when inactive) counts live bytes per thread only while an eval runs; the VM checks every 256 instructions and string/list repeat and concatenation and range check before allocating. Failure is a catchable error (memory limit exceeded (N MB)) that code inside the eval cannot swallow; nested evals are bounded by the parent's remaining cap. Precision limits documented: requested bytes not RSS; up to about 2x overshoot; other threads not counted. 14 new tests; release timings within noise of the old binary.

title: README audit link, libc claim corrected, cargo audit in CI
description: NCC audit sentence now links the chacha20poly1305 crate README (the crate README itself states the NCC Group audit); only chacha20poly1305 is called audited. The claim zero external dependencies was wrong on Unix (libc is a dependency for the JIT): README, CRYPTO, CHANGELOG and Cargo.toml comments now say so. Cargo.lock is tracked. New CI job cargo audit runs against Cargo.lock.

title: Eval memory cap allocator moved from the library to the CLI binaries; mem-cap feature
description: The counting allocator is no longer installed by the library: memcap::CountingAlloc is an opt-in type, unsafe_code is allowed only on its impl, and the killer, killer_super, killer-native and killer-repl binaries declare it themselves (cfg not mem-cap). New optional Cargo feature mem-cap makes the library install it for embedders. memcap::is_installed() reports whether the counter works; without it the live-memory check does not exist and only pre-checks, step and time budgets apply. New tests eval_memory_embedded (5) and eval_memory_cli (2); eval_memory tests declare the allocator. Docs, FEATURES and CHANGELOG updated.
